items.title: Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: I mean a perfect example is I mean I guess my all-time favorite classical composer, musician, is Bartok.

ctx.x: Okay. I wonder if you have ever attended a concert, let’s say someone like Albert Ayler who was on the far end of where things could go, and witnessed a reaction like the audience at the premier of “The Rite of Spring”?

Well you know those fellows, when they were creating that free form thing, and I watched that because I broke in right at the same time, there wasn’t an audience really. There was like a few family and friends. And you know the writers in the magazines gave it a big lift you know. And then people started to say well what is this all about, and started to come. And there were two places on the Lower East Side where this was incubated and really got going. And one was called a speakeasy. Actually that place is…

mean for the beboppers, so-called straight ahead guys, you know some of it got incorporated into, you know, the mainstream of things. And just like with classical music you know, things got worked out. I mean a perfect example is I mean I guess my all-time favorite classical composer, musician, is Bartok. And the reason why is not only is his works, you know, just out of this world great, but you know he said you know I’m really a Bach guy. You know? But he took that and did like what happened with all our form,…
